ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show fee; no refund to the rider. Note the NS-9 flag: this is the rider's 3rd no-show cancellation in a rolling 30-day window.
ruling.reasoning:
The driver is the cancelling party, so NS-0 sends the case to the NS-1 / NS-2 branch: driver cancelled, app reason rider_no_show, and the rider's own account is "I came out a minute after the driver cancelled" [F4]. The rider does not claim the driver gave some other reason, so the only live question is whether NS-1's four conditions hold [NS-0].

NS-1(i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:57:00 while 40 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach was 38 m, well within the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(ii) is satisfied: he then remained at the pickup continuously for 6 min 0 s before cancelling at 13:03:00, exceeding both the 5-minute free wait and the later-of-arrival/scheduled-time count (arrival 12:57:00 is the later of the two) [F3][F6][F7][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) is satisfied: before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 12:57:30) and made 1 in-app call (12:58:30) [F5][F13][NS-1]. NS-1(iv) is satisfied: the GPS shows him stationary 12:57:00–13:03:00 at a point 40 m from pickup, so there is no presence gap and nothing to escalate under TH-4 [F3][NS-1].

The NS-0:reason element is met. The app reason is rider_no_show, and his own words give no reason of his own: "At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel." at 12:57, "Waited more than 5 min, cancelling" at 13:02, and his written statement "I pressed I'm Here and waited more than 5 minutes. Rider no-show, so I cancelled." [F4][F10][F11][F12][F14]. His messages are exclusively about waiting for and then cancelling on a non-appearing rider. That is why the fee stands, and this is the outcome the trace requires [NS-0][NS-1].

Amount: the cancellation fee on record is $5.00 [F8]. Because NS-1 holds, no amount is refundable under NS-2, and no other charge is in dispute; there is no deviation or surge component (1.0× multiplier) to compute [F8][F9][RD-2][SURGE-2]. The NS-1 conditions all pass in the trace, so the fee is upheld and the amount is null.

The safety screen found nothing. I read all three chat/statement items in context: "At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel." and "Waited more than 5 min, cancelling" are a location notice and a wait notice, and the statement "I pressed I'm Here and waited more than 5 minutes. Rider no-show, so I cancelled." is a factual account of the cancellation; the complaint "I came out a minute after the driver cancelled. I was charged $5.00 for nothing." contains an accusation of unfair charging, not a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F10][F11][F14][F4]. No safety issue arises, so no escalation under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2.

Evidence is sufficient: GPS coverage of the arrival and wait window, timestamped messages, the call log and the cancellation record settle every element the ruling needs, so there is no gap [F1][F2][F3][F4][F5][F6][F12][F13][TH-4].

On the flag: the profile shows 2 prior no-show cancellations in the 30 days before this one, and this cancellation is a third, so NS-9's threshold of 3 or more in a rolling 30-day window is reached [F18][NS-9]. That clause is recorded in the structured field, not in the ruling itself. The rider is a repeat no-show, not the driver; nothing shows a fraudulent arrival mark, so no NS-2 flag applies [F1][F7][NS-2]. The profiles do not decide the case: the driver's record (3 disputes, 2 upheld) and the rider's do not alter the NS-1 outcome [F18][F19].
